newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crudes gain momentum late, aided by arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crudes gain momentum late, aided by arb.

text.p: U.S. sweet grades gained momentum Tuesday in a flurry of activity spurred by the narrow Atlantic arbitrage, traders said.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.30-40 a barrel, even against Monday's cash level.
Five confirmed deals for Light Louisiana Sweet/St James ranged from 75 cents to 83 cents premium over WTI/Cushing, up about five cents from Monday.
One deal for Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was confirmed at plus 79 cents, and another confidential deal was pegged at plus 85 cents. This range was up around six cents from Monday.
The Dec/Jan WTI spread narrowed slightly to 10 cents, pushing down WTI/Cushing Posting Plus to 1.80/1.81 a barrel, down from yesterday's $1.93-1.82 range.
In contrast to sweets, sour grades languished.
"The sours weakened because of the sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and ample U.S. inventories," a Northeast trader said.
Three deals for West Texas Sour/Midland ranged from minus $1.64-1.61, down slightly from minus $1.60 last week.
WTI/Midland apparently saw no takers, with the grade notionally pegged at plus 3-4 cents.
Traders said the grade might be cast aside after a rumor filtered into the market one refiner had picked up a million barrels of mid-Dec arrival Brent. The sale could not be immediately confirmed.
